speaker: Doctor
text: Glad the CBC is normal. Since your blood glucose results weren't provided yet, are you aware of any history with diabetes or high blood sugar? Also, does the wound have a distinct shape like a "punched-out" ulcer, or is it irregular?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That family history of swelling is concerning for chronic venous insufficiency. Given your past DVT and the duration of the swelling, do you experience pain or heaviness in the leg that worsens when standing and improves with elevation? Also, have you noticed any skin discoloration (brownish staining) or hardening of the skin around the wound?

REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer, Venous Doppler Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up photos of the wound edges and surrounding skin texture

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer secondary to Chronic Venous Insufficiency with history of DVT.

Based on your history of DVT, family history of leg swelling, and the 6-month duration of the wound, the clinical picture strongly points to chronic venous insufficiency causing skin breakdown. The normal CBC rules out active infection, but we need to confirm the venous pathology with the upcoming ultrasound to guide compression therapy.
